title: Residual five Korean forms: candidate-only resolution map

cases.observedRelation: The exact string is attested as the title/label of a Cheolma-myeon folk song in a local-culture PDF; that proves an attested title use, not a dictionary lexeme or a transparent morpheme boundary.
cases.why: A source-backed exact-string use exists as a regional folk-song title, but it does not establish whether the title is compositional, dialectal, playful, or opaque. Do not infer a 칡+칡+이 parse from the title.
cases.nextEvidence: Obtain the cited 양산의 민요 (1992), p. 180 or a rights-cleared reliable transcription with surrounding field notes; determine whether 칡칡이 is a lexicalized title, a refrain/onomatopoeic form, or morphologically analyzable. Until then keep strict-mode abstention.

evidence.scope: The PDF lists 칡칡이 as the heading for 철마면 민요 26, with singer/date/location metadata and a citation to 이소라, 양산의 민요 (1992), p. 180. It does not provide a lexical gloss or morpheme segmentation.

cases.observedRelation: 쫒 is one consonant away from the attested standard lexeme 쫓다; this is a spelling relation, not a phonological rule.
cases.productionAction: Do not alter the input or clear strict-mode abstention. A separate spelling-assistance UI may show the candidate.

evidence.scope: The Korean Basic Dictionary supports 쫓아내다 and its standard surface pronunciation [쪼차내다], not a literal pronunciation of misspelled 쫒아내면.

cases.nextEvidence: If user confirms the correction, analyze 쫓아내면 as the corrected input through the normal source-phonology → IPA → Ukrainian pipeline; independently verify broad IPA before accepting a Ukrainian target.

cases.observedRelation: There are at least two independent uncertainties: 앗 versus standard past-tense 았, and whether final 유유유 is literal syllabic text or intended crying emoticon ㅠㅠㅠ.

candidateForms.normalization: 앗→았; 유유유→ㅠㅠㅠ with a token boundary

cases.productionAction: Keep all candidates separate from the original. Do not treat expressive ㅠㅠㅠ as Korean lexical syllables or discard it without a candidate label.

evidence.scope: The NIKL answer contains standard spelling 많았구나 in a quotation; it does not adjudicate this noisy token or its final sequence.

A published interview explicitly explains ㅠㅠㅠ as 'tears' and separately describes 유유유 as a title/phrase meaning 'you you you'. This demonstrates that the strings can have different interpretations in different contexts; it does not identify the intended meaning in the user's isolated input.

cases.nextEvidence: User/context confirmation of whether the tail is ㅠㅠㅠ, literal 유유유, or a separate token; then analyze the confirmed Korean span only.

cases.observedRelation: NIKL explicitly permits the surface readings [살믜] and [살메] for the particle phrase. These Hangul readings constrain the candidate set but are not IPA transcriptions.
cases.productionAction: Keep both candidates visible only in diagnostic/review output; accepted Ukrainian target remains withheld.

evidence.scope: Official Hangul surface-pronunciation alternatives [살믜]/[살메], not independently adjudicated IPA.

cases.nextEvidence: Two independent qualified reviewers annotate broad IPA, syllable boundary, and variant status blind to engine output; reconcile disagreements; then conduct a separate Ukrainian-target review on frozen IPA.

cases.observedRelation: Likely spelling correction 웟→웠 in the standard form 무서웠어; do not silently rewrite the original.
cases.productionAction: Do not alter the input or clear strict-mode abstention. A separate spelling-assistance UI may show the candidate.

evidence.scope: The Korean Basic Dictionary attests the standard spelling 무서웠어 in an example, not automatic normalization of 무서웟어.

cases.nextEvidence: If user confirms the correction, analyze the corrected form through the existing IPA-first path and independently review the resulting IPA and Ukrainian target.
